Condition : 1 - Development shall be carried out in all respects in accordance with the proposals contained in this application and the drawings and documents submitted, unless otherwise specified in other conditions attached to this consent:
Energy Statement (12869, Rev 2, February 2026), received 18/02/2026.
Drawing '02.SURVEY AND SITE PROPOSAL OUTLINE_REV F', received 26/01/2026.
Transport Technical Note (003, issue 01, dated November 2025), received 19/11/2025.
Drawing '03_Rev 03', received 22/09/2025.
Drawing '06.ACCESS TO SITE rev.01', received 19/08/2025.
Drawings '01.SURVEY AFTER CHANGE OF LEVELS', '04_Rev 02' ROOF PLAN, '05_Rev 02' ELEVATIONS, Site Location Plan and unnumbered existing site plan, and completed LBH Drainage Assessment Form, Preliminary Ecological Appraisal (240558-ED-01, dated August 2025), Preliminary Fire Safety Strategy (dated 20 June 2025), Transport Statement (001, issue 02, dated January 2025) and Travel Plan (002, issue 02, dated January 2025), received 25/07/2025.
All unlawful items not included within this permission shall be regularised and removed within three months of this decision.
Reason: To ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.
Condition : 2 - Notwithstanding the details on the approved plans, within three months of this decision, full and finalised details of all hard and soft landscaping features shall have been submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing, including a finalised landscaping plan indicating all landscaping features on a single plan. 
Hard landscaping details shall include: 
�	proposed finished levels or contours;
�	means of enclosure, including boundary treatment and gates (with supporting section/elevation drawings and specifications/materials);
�	car parking final layouts; 
�	other vehicle and pedestrian access and circulation areas; 
�	hard surfacing material(s); 
�	minor artefacts and structures (e.g. street furniture, refuse / cycle or other storage units, signs etc.); 
�	finalised lighting locations/specifications/plans;
�	proposed and existing functional services above and below ground (eg drainage power, communications cables, pipelines etc. indicating lines, manholes, supports etc.);
�	details of all renewable energy technologies, including the specifications (regarding power), number, appearance, location, orientation, total area and predicted carbon savings from the photovoltaic panels, and confirmation that the photovoltaic panels will be installed in accordance with the approved details and retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development.
Soft landscape details shall include:
�	schedules of trees and plants, noting species, plant sizes and proposed numbers/densities where appropriate, including for any planting boxes; 
�	written specifications (including cultivation and other operations associated with plant and grass establishment); 
�	an implementation and management / maintenance programme.
Development shall be carried out in accordance with these details and the landscaping provisions shall be retained as such thereafter.

Condition : 3 - Within six months of this decision, evidence of compliance with the recommendations of the Preliminary Ecological Appraisal (240558-ED-01, dated August 2025) hereby approved shall have been submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing. This shall include the findings of the further bat, reptile and badger inspections mentioned in the document (and any necessary protection or enhancement measures), and evidence of measures taken to eliminate invasive species across the site, including a schedule of works for continuing these eradication works in the event that the invasive species still remain at the site within the six month period from decision. 
This evidence shall also include an Ecological Management Plan (EMP) which incorporates:
�	finalised details of ecological enhancement, including biodiversity net gains (plus supporting biometric calculations/ area habitat summary) and urban greening factor;
�	details of how the enhancement measures will be monitored, managed and maintained, including the long-term design objectives, management responsibilities and maintenance schedules;
�	details on the location and type (including specifications) of bird boxes and other appropriate ecological enhancements (e.g. nest boxes / bricks / cups for house martins and swifts etc.; bat boxes; insect blocks; newt habitat improvements; reptile log piles; hedgehog houses etc.), in addition to maintenance provisions and a commitment that any data collected is to be shared with the Council;
�	species surveys within and around the site to demonstrate ecological enhancements;
�	an ecological lighting plan / strategy showing how any lighting on site would be designed to avoid harm to existing and future ecology on site (e.g. light intensity and hours of use).
The development shall then be carried out in strict accordance with the approved details.
Reason: In the interest of maintaining existing ecology at the site and delivering biodiversity enhancements.
Condition : 4 - The use of the premises shall be limited exclusively to sports-related purposes falling within Use Class F2, and shall be used for no other purpose. This includes any other purpose within Class F2 of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended) which would be incompatible with the Green Belt or any provision equivalent to that Class in any statutory instrument revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification.
Reason: The Council is satisfied that the use hereby permitted would not result in detriment to adjoining properties but would wish to control future changes of use within the same Use Class to protect nearby land uses and the character of the area.
Condition : 5 - Within three months of the date of this decision, the applicant shall have notified the Grounds Management Association (GMA) Regional Pitch Advisor and have enabled them to assess the Football pitch quality and condition to provide a report relating to its quality. If the Football pitch quality falls below Performance Quality Standards (PQS) requirements, the applicant will be required to set out recommendations, a schedule of works and a timescale to bring the Football pitch up to the required quality. The Football pitch shall thereafter be maintained to this quality for as long as the development hereby permitted remains in existence. 
Reason: To ensure that the playing pitch is prepared and maintained to an adequate standard and is fit for purpose in order to justify the rest of the development being acceptable in Green Belt terms, in accordance with Development Plan policies. 
Supporting notes: 
The applicant is advised that the scheme should comply with the relevant industry Technical Guidance, including guidance published by Sport England and Football Association. 
The applicant is also advised to engage with Middlesex Football Association to facilitate a GMA Reginal Pitch Advisor visit.
Condition : 6 - Within three months of this permission, a soil verification report, verifying that disturbed and redeposited materials are suitable for the proposed use and do not pose an unacceptable risk to human health, shall have been submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing. The report shall be prepared by a suitably qualified and experienced person. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and used with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes:
(i)	The site is located on a former landfill and the application is retrospective in nature. Surplus excavated materials appear to have been deposited within areas of raised ground / shallow embankments formed along parts of the site. Given the former landfill use and the potential for heterogeneous Made Ground to have been disturbed and relocated during cut-and-fill operations, there is a need to verify that disturbed and redeposited materials are suitable for the proposed use and do not pose an unacceptable risk to human health. Where applicable, the report shall describe how any additional/unexpected contamination encountered during development has been managed.
(ii)	This report shall demonstrate that the development is suitable for its proposed use in terms of land quality.
(iii)	The Council requests that the verification report or site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.
Condition : 7 - a) The development hereby approved shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Energy Statement.
b) Within six months of this decision, evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and to include As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure/National Calculation Method) shall have been submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing to show that the development has been constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy, and any subsequent approved revisions.
Reason: To ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.
Condition : 8 - Notwithstanding the submitted information and within three months of this decision, full details of the arrangements for the storing of waste and recycled materials (including details of how the placing of waste and recycled materials in a suitable location for collection would be undertaken and managed, with capacity to meet the requirements of the Council's Recycling and Refuse Guidelines SPD) shall have been submitted to for approval in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the approved details. 
Reason: In order to ensure adequate provision for waste and recycling, protect the quality of the local environment and prevent obstruction and inconvenience to users of the development.
Condition : 9 - Notwithstanding the submitted information and within three months of this decision, full details (including the number, location, design of structure and manufacturer's specifications of both long and short stay provisions) of all 32 cycle stands hereby approved shall have been submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing by. 
The approved facilities shall be fully implemented and made available for use within three months of that approval and thereafter retained for use at all times without obstruction.
Reason: To support sustainable transport objectives.
Condition : 10 - The four active electric vehicle charging points and five passive electric vehicle charging points as shown on the approved plans and documents, each capable of a minimum output of 7.2kW, shall be installed and all active charging points made ready for use within six months of this decision and shall be retained permanently and in good order thereafter.
Reason: In order to promote sustainable modes of transport.
Condition : 11 - The two disabled car parking bays as shown on the approved plans and documents shall be installed and made available and accessible within six months of this decision and shall be permanently retained as such thereafter.
Reason: In order to promote sustainable modes of transport.
Condition : 12 - Notwithstanding the submitted details, within three months of the date of this decision a finalised Parking Management Plan shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall include the following: 
�	details of measures to restrict parking to the 29 designated bays shown on the approved plans only, including how this provision will be operated and how parking outside the marked bays (e.g. elsewhere on site or at the neighbouring site) will be prohibited and enforced;
�	specifications of all bus parking, EV and blue badge spaces, and a commitment to convert passive EV bays to active and to provide additional Blue Badge bays when demand requires;
�	details of the operation of any gates or barriers;
�	details of how parking will be monitored and managed;
�	measures to ensure that all relevant parties are informed of the Parking Management Plan.
Thereafter the approved details shall have been fully implemented and made available for use within three months of that approval and thereafter retained for those purposes at all times without obstruction 
Reason: To promote sustainable modes of transport and ensure that the scheme does not give rise to highway safety concerns.
Condition : 13 - Within three months of this decision, a Delivery and Servicing Plan (including details of vehicle access and egress arrangements and times that servicing shall take place) shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall accord with current guidance such as that issued by TfL and include measures required to ensure sufficient arrangements (physical as well as managerial) for the servicing, including refuse collection, of all aspects of the development, the timing of hours for deliveries by motor vehicles and a timetable for implementation. 
Within three months of the date of that approval the development shall not be operated otherwise than in accordance with the approved details and shall be maintained for the lifetime of the development
Reason: In the interests of the safety of pedestrians and vehicles, to protect neighbours' living conditions and to support sustainable transport objectives.
description: Part retrospective application for the erection of a single storey sports clubhouse and the change of use from the keeping of horses to outdoor sport and recreation, including engineering operations to create level ground for the laying out of a grass football pitch, together with associated car parking, cycle storage and associated ancillary works.
subdivision_of_building: Most of the buildings associated with the use as a stables were demolished following storm damage. One storage building remains, see plan of site as existing and proposed.
